scenes.tts: Touch and pain enter the cord by the same root. How can one cut remove touch on one side, pain on the other?
scenes.visual: A body outline with the right leg touched and pricked. Both signals enter one dorsal root. The question on screen.
scenes.narration: Touch and pain enter the cord by the same root. How can one cut remove touch on one side, pain on the other?

scenes.tts: Picture a slice through the cord, back at the top. Touch runs in blue, pain in red.
scenes.visual: A cord cross-section: grey butterfly inside white matter. Label: dorsal (toward the back) at the top. A blue line and a red line enter from a root on the right side.
scenes.narration: Picture a slice through the cord, back at the top. Touch runs in blue, pain in red.

scenes.tts: The blue line carries fine touch, vibration and position sense.
scenes.visual: Blue line labelled: dorsal column-medial lemniscus pathway. Fine touch, vibration, position sense.
scenes.narration: The blue line carries fine touch, vibration and position sense.

scenes.tts: Its main branch climbs on its own side, with no synapse until the medulla. Other branches synapse in the dorsal horn.
scenes.visual: The main blue branch rises in the right dorsal column, labelled ipsilateral (same side), up to the caudal medulla. Small side branches end in the dorsal horn at entry.
scenes.narration: Its main branch climbs on its own side, with no synapse until the medulla. Other branches synapse in the dorsal horn.

scenes.tts: There, a second axon crosses and climbs to the thalamus. A thalamic neuron relays the signal to cortex.
scenes.visual: At the gracile or cuneate nucleus a second axon crosses as internal arcuate fibres, forms the medial lemniscus, and ends in the thalamus. A separate thalamic neuron carries the signal on to somatosensory cortex.
scenes.narration: There, a second axon crosses and climbs to the thalamus. A thalamic neuron relays the signal to cortex.

scenes.tts: So the blue line crosses in the medulla.
scenes.visual: Marker on the blue crossing: crosses in the medulla.
scenes.narration: So the blue line crosses in the medulla.

scenes.tts: The red line carries pain and temperature.
scenes.visual: Red line labelled: spinothalamic pathway. Pain and temperature.
scenes.narration: The red line carries pain and temperature.

scenes.tts: Its sensory axon synapses in the dorsal horn, near where it entered.
scenes.visual: The red sensory axon sends short branches up and down in Lissauer's tract, then synapses in the dorsal horn near its entry segment.
scenes.narration: Its sensory axon synapses in the dorsal horn, near where it entered.

scenes.tts: The next axon crosses within a segment or two, and climbs the opposite side.
scenes.visual: The second red axon crosses in the anterior white commissure and rises in the left anterolateral cord, labelled contralateral (opposite side), to the thalamus.
scenes.narration: The next axon crosses within a segment or two, and climbs the opposite side.

scenes.tts: So the red line crosses in the spinal cord.
scenes.visual: Marker on the red crossing: crosses in the spinal cord.
scenes.narration: So the red line crosses in the spinal cord.

scenes.tts: Now cut the right half of the cord at the tenth thoracic segment. Which side loses touch, and which loses pain?
scenes.caption: Now cut the right half of the cord at the tenth thoracic segment, T10. Which side loses touch, and which loses pain?
scenes.visual: A segment ruler from T9 to T12 beside the cord. A cut through the right half at T10. The question on screen.
scenes.narration: Now cut the right half of the cord at the tenth thoracic segment, T10. Which side loses touch, and which loses pain?

scenes.tts: Fine touch, vibration and position sense are lost on the right. The blue line has not crossed yet.
scenes.visual: The body outline shades blue on the right below T10. Label: fine touch, vibration and position sense lost.
scenes.narration: Fine touch, vibration and position sense are lost on the right. The blue line has not crossed yet.

scenes.tts: Pain is lost on the left. The red fibres in the right half have already crossed from the left.
scenes.visual: The body outline shades red on the left, starting a little below the cut.
scenes.narration: Pain is lost on the left. The red fibres in the right half have already crossed from the left.

scenes.tts: Now look closer. Follow one left pain fibre entering one segment below the cut.
scenes.visual: Zoom on the ruler: one red fibre enters on the left at T11.
scenes.narration: Now look closer. Follow one left pain fibre entering one segment below the cut.

scenes.tts: In this simple example, its pathway reaches the other side a segment or two higher.
scenes.visual: Two dashed options for the crossing, labelled illustrative: at T10 or at T9.
scenes.narration: In this simple example, its pathway reaches the other side a segment or two higher.

scenes.tts: Crossing at the cut, it is lost. Crossing above the cut, it is spared.
scenes.visual: Crossing at T10 runs into the cut: lost. Crossing at T9 reaches the right side above the cut: spared.
scenes.narration: Crossing at the cut, it is lost. Crossing above the cut, it is spared.

scenes.tts: So the pain loss on the left begins one or two segments below the cut.
scenes.visual: The red shading on the left starts at about T11 to T12.
scenes.narration: So the pain loss on the left begins one or two segments below the cut.

scenes.tts: On the right, at the cut itself, a narrow band can lose sensation too. The cut damages the sensory fibres entering there, and the dorsal horn they reach.
scenes.visual: A thin band on the right at the cut level shades both blue and red. Label: segmental sensory loss, schematic.
scenes.narration: On the right, at the cut itself, a narrow band can lose sensation too. The cut damages the sensory fibres entering there, and the dorsal horn they reach.

scenes.tts: Fine touch lost on one side and pain on the other is the core of the Brown Say-car pattern.
scenes.caption: Fine touch lost on one side and pain on the other is the core of the Brown-Séquard pattern.
scenes.visual: Label: the Brown-Séquard pattern. Fine touch and strength lost on one side, pain on the other.
scenes.narration: Fine touch lost on one side and pain on the other is the core of the Brown-Séquard pattern.

scenes.tts: Run it backwards. Pain is lost in the right leg, vibration in the left. Which half of the cord is cut?
scenes.visual: A new body outline: red shading on the right leg, blue on the left. The question on screen.
scenes.narration: Run it backwards. Pain is lost in the right leg, vibration in the left. Which half of the cord is cut?

scenes.tts: The left half. Vibration rides the blue line, which stays on its own side.
scenes.visual: The left half of the cord darkens. The blue line on the left is severed; crossed red fibres from the right run through the same cut.
scenes.narration: The left half. Vibration rides the blue line, which stays on its own side.

scenes.tts: For these two routes, where a line crosses tells you where the damage is.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: for the dorsal column and spinothalamic routes from the body, blue crosses in the medulla and red crosses in the cord. The side of a deficit locates the lesion.
scenes.narration: For these two routes, where a line crosses tells you where the damage is.
